properties.title: Starlink still restricted for Ukraine despite Trump saying Musk lifted speed limits
properties.description: KYIV — Ukrainian interceptors still cannot use the internet at high speed to shoot down Russian attack drones or conduct mid-strike operations as of Friday morning, Ukrainian officials and a drone operator said, despite U.S. President Donald Trump saying SpaceX founder Elon Musk had lifted speed restrictions on his Starshield service. “Morning tests show the speed limits of 140–160 km/h are still there, and the navigation isn’t working properly,” a Ukrainian government official told POLITICO on condition of anonymity. “As of this morning, instances of connectivity loss at speeds of 161 km/h are still being observed. properties.title: The EU heads into a perfect political storm
properties.description: The EU heads into a perfect political storm Last week’s summit gave Brussels a taste of how hard it’s going to be to get a deal on the budget — or anything else. By SEBASTIAN STARCEVIC in Brussels Illustration by Natália Delgado / POLITICO The EU is already struggling with how to get its largest-ever budget agreed, plug a massive financial hole for Ukraine and navigate geopolitical pressure from the U.S. and China. properties.title: Ukraine strikes oil facility in St. Petersburg as part of ‘massive’ drone attack
properties.description: Ukraine struck an oil terminal in St. Petersburg Sunday morning in what Russian state media called “one of the biggest drone attacks of the year.” Alexander Beglov, governor of St. Petersburg, said on Telegram Sunday that the city underwent a “massive” overnight attack from Ukrainian drones. “The Ministry of Emergency Situations continues to extinguish fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal, the Ruchyi oil depot, and industrial warehouses in the Kolpino district,” he said, adding that one person died and several others were injured in the incident. The drone strikes come as Kyiv and Moscow ramp up attacks on each other’s infrastructure.
